speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have swelling and pain in your right ring finger; have you noticed any recent trauma to that area, or is this appearing gradually? Are you experiencing fever, chills, or redness spreading beyond the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the mechanism of injury suggests a tendon rupture or fracture. Did you hear a "pop" at the moment of injury, and can you actively flex or extend that finger against resistance? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger. The patient describes a classic presentation of a mallet finger (inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, extension lag at rest) following a specific trauma mechanism where the finger was forcibly extended or pulled, likely causing an avulsion fracture or tendon rupture. The mention of pyelonephritis is clinically irrelevant to a hand injury.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
